condition: subacute unexplained drenching night sweats soaking bedsheets 4 nights weekly with unintentional 5 kg weight loss over 6 weeks
level_rationale: Six weeks of unexplained 5 kg unintentional weight loss accompanied by drenching night sweats soaking the bedsheets 4 nights a week in a 44-year-old man describes classic subacute systemic B-symptoms warranting a prompt outpatient physician visit for targeted history, lymph-node and abdominal examination, laboratory workup, and chest imaging rather than self-care or immediate emergency resuscitation, whereas developing an acute 104 F fever tonight with violent shaking chills and inability to stand up on top of 6 weeks of unexplained weight loss signals acute febrile sepsis or hematologic decompensation requiring immediate emergency department evaluation.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult non-native everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + Rule A constitutional B-symptom to acute febrile rigor and orthostatic collapse escalation control (-cf, L2 to L4), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover a 44-year-old man, 5 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 weeks, and drenching night sweats soaking his bedsheets 4 nights a week over those 6 weeks without naming lymphoma or tuberculosis and without contractions, with an exact 0-word span difference (13 vs 13 words). Under Rules A and D, escalating f3 inside the same constitutional illness to an acute 104 F fever tonight with violent shaking chills and inability to stand up avoids leaving 5 kg unexplained weight loss stranded on a benign control and moves care cleanly from outpatient physician workup (level 2) to emergency evaluation (level 4).
